message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Step | What Happens | Key Points | |------|--------------|------------| | **1. Setup** | • Shuffle the Uno deck (108 cards).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | • If the first card is an action card, its effect applies to the first player (e.g., Skip, Reverse, Draw Two, Wild). | | **2. Turn Order** | • Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a Reverse card is played). | • The direction changes only when a Reverse card is played. | | **3. Playing a Card** | • On your turn, you may play one card from your hand that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top discard card.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile. | • You may play a Wild or Wild Draw Four at any time (subject to the “no‑penalty” rule). | | **4. Action Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – Player chooses the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – Player chooses the next color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. | • Wild Draw Four can only be played if you have no other playable card (unless challenged). | | **5. Drawing** | • If you draw a card that can be played immediately, you may play it on the same turn. | • If you cannot play the drawn card, your turn ends. | | **6. Calling “Uno”** | • When you have **exactly one card left**, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. | • Failure to call UNO before the next player’s turn ends results in a penalty: you must draw two cards. | | **7. Winning a Round** | • The round ends when a player discards all their cards.
• That player scores points based on the cards left in opponents’ hands: Number cards = face value, Draw Two/Reverse/Skip = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | • The first player to reach 500 points (or another agreed threshold) wins the game. | | **8. Penalties & Challenges** | • If a player plays a Wild Draw Four illegally, the next player can challenge. If the challenger is correct, the challenger draws four cards; if wrong, the challenger draws six. | • Only challenge if you suspect the player had a playable card of the current color. | --- ### Quick Tips - **Keep track of colors** – If you’re low on cards, try to keep a variety of colors so you can play more often. - **Use Wilds strategically** – Save Wild Draw Four for when you’re sure you’re out of matching colors. - **Watch the discard pile** – Knowing what cards have been played helps you anticipate opponents’ moves. Enjoy your game!
